# Gunman kills 6 in 'terror attack' in Krakow, Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
By Shayna Jacobs and Dennis Romero

(Fetch tool returned a condensed rendering of the article; text below is as returned.)

A shooter with far-right beliefs opened fire in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday, killing six people and injuring at least 15 others. Poland's defense minister characterized the midday attack as a "terror attack."

The gunman, a man in his mid-20s from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie (approximately 93 miles northeast of Krakow), fired from a moving vehicle using an automatic rifle. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński stated: "Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideologies."

Following the public shooting, three of the shooter's relatives were discovered dead in an apartment. Deputy Police Inspector Andrzej Fijołek identified them as "believed to be his parents and sister."

Prime Minister Donald Tusk praised two police officers wounded in the incident, calling them "true heroes." One officer sustained three gunshot wounds and underwent surgery. Tusk noted: "They likely saved lots of lives while risking their own lives."

Four of the six victims were identified as three Polish nationals and one British citizen. The injured include foreign nationals from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia, and Britain. The U.S. State Department confirmed no American citizens were harmed.

The attacker was shot by police at the scene and hospitalized around 3 p.m. local time. Police located additional weapons and ammunition in his vehicle. Krakow announced a mourning period through November 11.

U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose wrote on social media: "America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens."
